title: Customizing Cache Indexing Through Entropy Estimation
problem: Cache indexing has received limited research attention compared to replacement and prefetching strategies, yet sits in the critical performance path. Previous indexing schemes either provide moderate performance or incur prohibitively expensive computational delays, failing to satisfy both performance and efficiency requirements simultaneously.
motivation: Cache management is fundamental to achieving high performance in modern computers, making efficient and fast cache indexing critical for overall system performance.
method: ENTROPyINDEX observes which bits of the memory address change most during cache misses—a measurement called entropy, or degree of variation. It then selects the address bits that vary the most, since these will distribute cached data more evenly across the cache storage. Because different programs access memory differently, the scheme adapts its bit selection to match each program's unique patterns.
key_novelty: The innovation is using entropy (degree of variation) in address bits during cache misses to dynamically determine which bits index the cache.
contributions: A novel entropy-based cache indexing scheme that dynamically adapts to application behavior at runtime
Achieves 3.39% geometric mean IPC improvement (up to 52.2% maximum) over power-of-two modulo baseline without prefetching
Outperforms state-of-the-art indexing schemes (PRIME, XORHASH) across SPEC 2006/2017, PARSEC, GAP, and CVP benchmarks
Maintains minimal computational overhead while demonstrating substantial gains on non-uniform workloads (5.58% speedup) and with prefetching enabled

metrics.speedup: 3.39% geometric mean IPC improvement without prefetching; 1.42% with prefetching; up to 5.58% on non-uniform workloads

primary_theme: Adaptive cache indexing through entropy estimation
